completed_scope: Publication queues exact repository/digest/size integrity work with references, journal and idempotency response; aliases deduplicate within one mutation and admission rejection rolls back all references. Existing outbox events become real verified source-event projections.

Tenant-scoped persisted lane budgets bound outstanding/running work, attempts and exponential retry. Independent execution slots and local round robin across configured identities preserve the implemented event/integrity lanes.

Dedicated worker credentials cannot access public APIs; public/admin tokens cannot execute worker work. Every operation reauthenticates after the tenant lock using actual current database time. Forced RLS/nonowner runtime applies to jobs, policies, projections and observations.

Generation/token/worker/deadline fences protect heartbeat and completion, including after crash, cancellation, credential revocation or replacement. Job control is idempotent; attempt history and immutable observations survive redrive.

The event handler checks its source hash/link and commits a projection plus job state. Completion positions preserve late projections. The integrity handler uses bounded, paced, cancellable SHA-256 reads and records storage observations without changing content policy.

Queue policy, cancellation and emergency credential operations remain audited while outbox capacity is full. Source publication rejected by capacity abandons only its current lease, publishes nothing and permits immediate fenced retry after repair.

Native worker/API/CLI proof covers actual hard kill and reclaim, reserved event lane, second-tenant progression before backlog drain, policy independence, same-length corruption, bounded retries, repair, cancellation, saturation, credential rollover and registry restart.
Prior native npm/Python/OCI/Maven/generic and one pinned real Docker Hub/token/CloudFront journey replay against identical clean binaries.

retained_failures.cause: Source-sequence activity cursors could skip a slower earlier event completed later.
Transaction-start time allowed a waiting worker claim after its credential actually expired.
Queue rejection at source completion could retain a fetching lease despite rollback.

fixture_correction.cause: The initial fixture incorrectly assumed job IDs were globally unique; equal source sequence/event keys legitimately identify different tenant-local jobs.
fixture_correction.repair: Use a noncolliding exact-byte job key for cross-tenant absence, while separately verifying forced RLS. No production tenant leak was established.

limits: All 450 broad capabilities and 41 format families remain open; every broad readiness verdict is negative.
Builtin event projection and SHA-256 storage integrity only. No scanner/security approval, signature verification, webhook, replication, GC or migration execution is inferred.
Two tenants and native processes on one macOS arm64 host, PostgreSQL 16.15 and local CAS; no full multi-host fairness/scale, native Linux/Windows, S3 or production packaging qualification.
Integrity tasks cover new publication/cache-fill intent and explicit redrives, not a complete historical store sweep. That inventory/sweep remains required.

Current queue history is retained. Production migration/restore/retention, interrupted external outcomes, orphan/CAS reconciliation, upload/retrieval reapers, mixed traffic isolation and every later product stage remain required.
Activity projects source outbox events; credential/job-control events stay in authoritative audit without recursively generating work. Projections and observations never authorize downloads.
The real public provider proof remains one pinned Linux arm64 Docker Hub anonymous-token/CloudFront image; full provider/private credential/PKI/client/platform campaigns remain required.
